definition: You license your brand and menu to a local owner who opens and runs the outlets. You earn a fee and a royalty and carry little risk.
You share ownership, costs and revenues of the outlets with a local partner.
You own and run the outlets yourself, keeping all revenue but carrying all costs and risks.
The chance that political, economic or legal problems in a country hurt your business.
Tariffs, quotas and rules that make importing goods or entering a market harder.
How intensely competitors fight for the same customers in a market.
How different a country's culture and habits are from your home country.
How freely a society allows enjoyment, leisure and spending on pleasure.
A country's economic output divided by its population; a rough measure of income.
The price of one currency in another. A weaker local currency shrinks profits when converted to dollars.
A tax charged on imported goods.
A regular payment, usually a percentage of sales, paid by a franchisee for using your brand.
A rule or choice to buy ingredients from suppliers inside the country.
The money you can allocate in a round.
Money in your pool that you did not allocate. It earns nothing but stays available.
The total of your profit and loss across all rounds played so far.
